title: Expose the running build's identity (source commit and binary hash) in /api/health so a remote host can be attested
outcome: Expose the running build's identity (source commit and binary hash) in /api/health so a remote host can be attested
acceptance: GET /api/health preserves ok and serverInstanceId and adds buildIdentity = { schemaVersion: 1, buildCommit: 40-hex|null, sourceState: "clean"|"dirty"|"unknown", binarySha256: 64-hex|null, crateVersion, platform: {os, arch}, unavailable: { buildCommit?: reason, binarySha256?: reason } }. The full build-time commit uses precise existing Git HEAD/current-ref/packed-refs inputs resolved for main and linked worktrees; the index is included for advisory sourceState. Dirty state is explicitly advisory, and authoritative attestation combines the runtime binary hash with the installer clean-tree record and the registered-tree checks. No deliberately missing rerun input or unconditional build-script rerun is used.

The startup-open read-only current_exe handle is retained for the process; SHA-256 is measured lazily once off the async executor and outside the shared state lock, never by reopening the executable path or embedding a binary hash at build time. Changing runtime working directory or Git HEAD, or renaming the running image aside and installing a replacement before or after first measurement, does not change the running process identity. Unavailable commit/hash values are null with fixed reason codes git_unavailable, no_repository, exe_unreadable or hash_pending in unavailable. Missing/malformed source metadata and unreadable images fail explicitly; no runtime Git/compiler inference occurs. Older replies without buildIdentity still decode.

Automated route/subprocess regressions cover known and unavailable health fields, build-time commit stability, advisory dirty/unknown state and Windows rename-aside replacement before and after first measurement. Isolated main-checkout and linked-worktree fixtures verify rerun inputs exist, and two consecutive no-change builds prove build.rs does not rerun on the second build, with elapsed time recorded. Existing health/remote-client tests remain green; the full five-stage gate passes on the exact input with an independent Codex plus Claude review pair and no outstanding in-scope Medium-or-higher finding.
